title: Storytelling

script.script:
My husband told me on his deathbed that he had a second family.

A woman and a daughter in another state for fourteen years.

I was holding his hand when he said it.

He died forty minutes later.

I sat in the hospital room for two hours after they pulled the sheet over his face, trying to understand how the man I slept next to for thirty one years had a whole other life I never knew about.

Fourteen years.

I found her address in his phone three days after the funeral.

I drove four hours without telling anyone.

She opened the door and knew who I was immediately.

She invited me in and I sat at her kitchen table and she poured me coffee.

And we looked at each other for a long time before either of us spoke.

She said he used to talk about you.

He said you were the love of his life.

I said then why?

She said because he could not watch your body change, and he did not have the courage to tell you why or help you fix it.

She was sixty one years old.

Flat stomach.

Clear skin.

Bright eyes.

She looked ten years younger than me.

I said how.

She walked to her cabinet and pulled out a soft cotton pack and a dark glass bottle.

She said this is what Egyptian women have used for three thousand years to drain the sludge that menopause leaves behind.

She said the ricinoleic acid absorbs through the skin three and a half inches deep into the tissue, where the drainage channels are clogged.

Calms the inflammation keeping the channels shut.

Softens the hardened waste.

Compression holds it against the drainage center.

The heat widens the channels so the sludge moves through.

Every pill gets destroyed by stomach acid.

The pack is direct delivery while you sleep.

She said the brand is called Haven & Spool.

Cold pressed.

90% ricinoleic acid.

Hexane free.

USDA organic.

Organic cotton pack that feels like a warm hug.

Nothing to swallow.

I said there is no way a pack fixes what fourteen years of this did to me.

She said six weeks.

Watch.

I drove home with the Haven & Spool pack on my passenger seat.

Handed to me by another woman across her kitchen table.

Photos of my dead husband hung on her wall.

Week one I wore it every night.

Nothing dramatic.

But I woke up less puffy.

Week two the bloating that made me unbutton my pants after every meal started going down.

I went to the bathroom without straining for the first time in years.

Week three my face in the mirror looked different.

Tighter.

Less swollen.

I looked like a version of me I had not seen in a decade.

The woman in her kitchen.

She knew this version.

She maintained this version.

While I disappeared and blamed age for what was actually drainage backup.

Week four down eleven pounds of pure sludge.

No brain fog.

Energy past 2pm.

I put on a dress I had not worn since my forties.

I looked in the mirror and saw the woman he married.

The one he should have fought to keep instead of replacing with a copy who knew what I did not.

Week six my daughter came over for dinner.

She walked in and stopped in the hallway.

She said mama you look like your wedding photo.

I said I feel like her too.

She said what did you do.

I told her about the pack.

About the oil.

About what Egyptian women have known for three thousand years.

I did not tell her about the woman.

Did not tell her about the address.

Some things a daughter does not need to carry.

She ordered Haven & Spool that night at my kitchen table.

My sister saw me the following week and grabbed my arm and said what is happening to you.

I told her about the pack.

She ordered before I finished the sentence.

I did not drain the sludge for him.

He is gone.

I drained it because a woman I should hate showed me more honesty in one afternoon than my husband showed me in thirty one years.

She gave me the one thing he never did.

The information.

He spent fourteen years with the woman who maintained the body I lost because she knew something I did not.

She could have kept that secret.

She handed it to me across her kitchen table instead.

Maybe your body changed after menopause and never came back.

Maybe somebody who should have told you something never did.

Maybe you have been carrying sludge and calling it age and watching yourself disappear while the people around you stayed quiet.

Menopause sludge is real.

It is not your fault.

You cannot diet away sludge.

You have to drain it.

The brand is called Haven & Spool.

Cold pressed castor oil pack.

Worn overnight.

Nothing to swallow.

Washable.

Reusable.

One purchase that lasts for years.

50% off right now.

60 day money back guarantee.

If you do not feel a difference, every penny refunded.

The risk is on them.

The choice is on you.

They are a small company and they sell out constantly.

If the button is still there, go grab it now.

He took the secret to his grave.

She dug it up and handed it to me.

Now I am handing it to you
